correctness.rationale: Degree-three proper conflict-free coloring is equivalent to proper two-dynamic coloring: the three neighbor colors must not all coincide. Pairing consecutive ordered rung columns yields 84 legal states and 384 transitions; a length-n closed walk corresponds bijectively to a named coloring. The finite identity det(I-tA)=D(t) was independently certified by constructing all entries of A, computing all traces through power 84, applying all Newton identities to 85 characteristic coefficients, and separately multiplying the seven displayed polynomial factors; all coefficients agree, including high-degree zeros. Counts n=3..11 match independently. The 3-color local successor restrictions force exactly two 3-periodic sequences, giving 12 named 3-colorings iff 3|n; 3-,4-,5-column closed walk constructions cover every n>=3 with four colors. Strong connectivity and aperiodicity of the four-palette state graph plus the factored spectrum establish the unique Perron root and asymptotic. A finite *exhaustive exact* determinant calculation is legitimately sufficient for all n via the formal log determinant identity; small-n checks alone would not be.

originality.rationale: The chromatic-number dichotomy three iff three divides n was previously addressed in homogeneous/two-dynamic prism coloring. General proper conflict-free papers give definitions and bounds. The exact factored four-palette all-n generating function and optimum partition counts are not implied by a chromatic-number theorem and were not found in relevant Resultary graph-coloring records. The finite transfer construction is standard but the complete characteristic-factor computation is a new exact natural census to the best of knowledge.

value.rationale: This is a motivated, complete exact enumerator for an infinite and natural cubic graph family at its sharp chromatic-palette threshold, not merely another upper-bound construction. It distinguishes a constant optimum partition count on multiples of three from exponential growth on the other circumferences and determines every named four-coloring by a rational generating function.

final_claim: For P_n=C_n square K2, n>=3, four named colors with open-neighborhood proper conflict-free constraint have generating series sum_{n>=3}F4(n)t^n= -tD'(t)/D(t)-24t^2 for the explicitly factored degree-36 determinant D. The minimum palette is three iff 3|n, otherwise four; minimum unlabeled class partition counts are 2 or F4(n)/24. F4 has dominant exponential base approximately 5.0340418358.
limitations: For named palette four, no requirement to use all colors; no claim for arbitrary larger palettes or other graph products.
Strong connectivity/aperiodicity property checked on the finite transition digraph.
